question: The dominant-isoform switching question requires per-transcript (or per-exon) quantification, but the staged inputs contain only a gene-level Salmon count matrix (12,000 genes x 12 samples). Can transcript-level quantifications be staged — per-sample Salmon quant.sf/abundance.h5 files plus a transcript-to-gene map, or equivalently a transcript-by-sample count matrix with transcript IDs — and if so, for which of the 12 samples?

input.questionContext: Dataset: AD lesional vs control skin, 6 vs 6, unpaired, single batch, raw gene-level counts from Salmon; sample_01 has ~4x lower library size than the median. The files present are counts/counts.csv (gene-level, 12000 x 13) and metadata/metadata.csv (12 x 2: sample, condition). Gene-level counts aggregate all isoforms of a gene, so dominant-isoform switches (DTU / isoform-switching analysis, e.g. DRIMSeq, DEXSeq, IsoformSwitchAnalyzeR) cannot be inferred from them; the run name suggests transcript-usage data was intended. Please confirm whether transcript-level quantifications exist for these samples and can be added, or whether the question should be re-scoped to what gene-level counts can support (e.g. differential expression with the shallow sample handled).
